The dominant risk being underwritten is the November FOMC hike converting a VIX/MOVE divergence into simultaneous equity and credit repricing — GLD, SCHD, BRK.B, and IEF are all sized to provide meaningful portfolio damping if that scenario materializes.
diversificationNote: The 10-pick growth book spans five GICS sectors: Information Technology (CRWD, PANW, NET, AMD, MRVL, MU — six names, but deliberately diversified across cybersecurity, AI accelerators, networking, and memory — distinct end markets and value-chain positions), Communication Services (META), Health Care (TMO), Energy (MPC), and Financials/value (SPGI); within IT, the six names cover three distinct sub-segments (security platforms, compute silicon, and memory/interconnect), reducing single-factor concentration risk. The defensive sleeve spans four distinct exposures: hard assets/gold (GLD), quality dividend equity (SCHD), conglomerate cash fortress (BRK.B), intermediate duration Treasuries (IEF), and consumer staples dividend compounder (KO) — covering the full defensive spectrum of inflation hedge, quality factor, optionality, duration hedge, and pricing-power income.
